data.content_ref: inline:{"analogy":{"adopted_commitment_refs":[],"disanalogies":["A physical instrument has a fixed transduction bandwidth; a checklist can be revised, so the 'cue-set' boundary is endogenous to the evaluation design.","Expert intuition may include configural (non-compensatory) cue combination that a linear checklist cannot encode, even if every cue is present."],"overturn_conditions":["An evaluation in which the checklist is demonstrably broader than the expert's effective cue-set.","A demonstration that configural cues are irrelevant to the specific verifiable task."],"shared_structure":["Both a checklist and a measurement instrument are calibrated against a reference; reliability gain from the instrument is not independent of the reference's coverage.","Using the instrument does not grant the user access to cues the instrument cannot transduce."],"source_memory_refs":["SRC_008","SRC_001"],"transfer_claims":["Just as a voltmeter does not reveal a signal outside its bandwidth, a checklist does not reveal a cue outside its authored list.","Panel reliability gain over the expert is bounded by checklist coverage relative to the expert's effective cue-set."]},"claim":"A trained non-expert panel with an explicit checklist will not reliably beat a single expert on verifiable tasks, because a good checklist is a transcript of expert tacit knowledge; if the checklist contains the full cue-set the expert uses, the panel merely parrots the expert (no net gain in expectation); if the checklist omits expert-unique cues, the panel is reliably inferior on exactly the cases that differentiate expertise.","counterconditions":[{"case":"If the checklist is derived from a strictly larger, validated, external corpus of cues than any single expert possesses, the panel could exceed the expert.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If the expert's intuition has large systematic bias and the checklist comes from a less-biased source, the panel may beat the expert.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"},{"case":"If aggregation is across independently authored checklists (not one shared checklist), the logic changes.","checker_spec":null,"eval":"observation"}],"definitions":[],"derivation":[],"formalization_refs":[],"mechanism":"Checklists do not create new validity; they externalize and freeze a snapshot of someone's cue-list. The panel's apparent aggregation benefit comes from within-checklist variance reduction, not from independent discovery of the right answer. On verifiable tasks, the hard cases are exactly those where the decisive cue is not on the checklist, and the expert's implicit cue-list is strictly richer. Thus the panel's reliability is a convex combination of (i) easy cases where both succeed and (ii) hard cases where the expert wins; the panel can only match the expert, never exceed, given the same checklist author.","premises":[],"schema":"deepreason-reasoning-envelope-v1","scope":{"covers":[],"excludes":[]},"simulation_refs":[],"uncertainties":[]}
